title: Wage claim, oldest wage due only five months before the petition: far inside every reading

expect.why: Wages of workers fall under the one-year limit (312 ¶3: 'تتقادم بسنة واحدة ... المبالغ المستحقة للعمال'). 314 ¶1: 'ولا يحسب اليوم الاول وتكمل المدة بانقضاء آخر يوم منها': the day of the due date is not counted and the year is complete at the end of 2027-01-10. Under the five-year reading of 309 ¶1 the last day would be 2031-01-10; in time under both, so the outcome is settled.

title: Wage claim, one day before the first anniversary of the due date

expect.why: 314 ¶1: 'ولا يحسب اليوم الاول وتكمل المدة بانقضاء آخر يوم منها': day 1 is 2025-06-16, the one-year period of 312 ¶3 is complete at the end of 2026-06-15. Petition on 06-14 is one day before the last day. In time under 309 ¶1 (five years) too. The text does not say how a year is counted (calendar year assumed).

title: Wage claim filed on the anniversary of the due date: one-year reading on its last day, five-year reading far in time

expect.why: The text does not settle this: 312 ¶3 (one year for amounts due to workers for their work) and 309 ¶1 (five years for 'المرتبات والاجور') both reach wages. Under 312 ¶3 and 314 ¶1 ('تكمل المدة بانقضاء آخر يوم منها') the last day is 2026-06-15 and the petition is on it (lastDay); under 309 ¶1 the last day is 2030-06-15 and the petition is in time. Likelier reading, the specific one-year rule: last day 2026-06-15. A rule must warn, not decide.

title: Wage claim, one day after the first anniversary of the due date

expect.why: The text does not settle this: under 312 ¶3 (one year) the last day is 2026-06-15 and the petition is one day late; under 309 ¶1 (five years, wages and salaries) it is in time until 2030-06-15. Both texts are in the list and neither says which governs wages claimed by a worker. Likelier reading: 312 ¶3, last day 2026-06-15. Only the pleading of the debtor can raise it (321 ¶1).

title: Five-year edge across a leap day: calendar years against 1825 days

expect.why: 314 ¶1 counts 'بالايام لا بالساعات' and excludes the first day, but the text does not say whether a year is a calendar year or 365 days. 2024 is a leap year. Calendar reading of five years (309 ¶1): last day 2026-02-28, the petition is on it. Day-count reading (5 x 365 = 1825 days from 2021-02-28): last day 2026-02-27, the petition is late. Also the one-year reading of 312 ¶3 would make the claim late long ago. The text does not settle this; a rule must warn.

title: Wage claim, oldest wage due more than five years before: late under every reading

expect.why: Under 312 ¶3 (one year) the period ended in 2021-03-01; under 309 ¶1 ('يتقادم بخمس سنوات') it ended on 2025-03-01 (314 ¶1: first day not counted, complete at the end of the last day). Late under both readings. lastDay left out because the two readings give different dates. The court may not raise it of its own motion: 321 ¶1 'لا يجوز للمحكمة أن تقضى تلقائيا بالتقادم', it needs the plea of the debtor or of an interested person (321 ¶2: possible at any stage, even on appeal).

title: Five-year edge: the day after the last day under the five-year reading

expect.why: 309 ¶1 five years from 2021-06-15: first day not counted, complete at the end of 2026-06-15 (314 ¶1); the petition on 06-16 is one day after. Under 312 ¶3 (one year) it ended in 2022. Late under both readings, so the outcome is settled. lastDay left out because the readings differ (2022-06-15 or 2026-06-15).

title: Five-year edge: the day before, which only the five-year reading keeps in time

expect.why: The text does not settle this: under 309 ¶1 (five years) the last day is 2026-06-15 and the petition is one day before it; under 312 ¶3 (one year for amounts due to workers) the last day was 2022-06-15 and the claim is late. Likelier reading: the one-year rule, last day 2022-06-15 (alternative 2026-06-15). A rule must warn, not decide.

title: One-year last day falls on a Friday; petition on the Sunday after

expect.why: The one-year period of 312 ¶3 from 2025-06-12 is complete at the end of Friday 2026-06-12 (314 ¶1). 405 ¶4 ('يمدد الأجل إلى أول يوم عمل موالي') extends to the next working day but speaks of the periods 'المنصوص عليها في هذا القانون' (the procedure code), and 314 is silent on rest days. 405 ¶3 only refers to 'النصوص الجاري بها العمل' for the weekly rest days, so the texts given do not say which days they are (outside practice, Friday and Saturday): the text does not settle this. Last day 2026-06-12 if not extended (petition one day late), 2026-06-14 (Sunday, if Friday and Saturday are rest days) if extended (petition on the last day). Also the five-year reading of 309 ¶1 keeps it in time. A rule must warn.

title: One-year last day falls on 5 July, a possible official holiday; petition the day after

expect.why: The last day under 312 ¶3 and 314 ¶1 is 2026-07-05 (a Sunday). 405 ¶3 says official holidays are 'أيام الأعياد الرسمية' as laid down by 'النصوص الجاري بها العمل': the texts given do not list the holidays, so I cannot tell from them that 5 July is one (it is the national day in practice, from outside the texts). If it is, and 405 ¶4 applies to this limitation, the last day is 2026-07-06 and the petition is on it. The text does not settle this: last day 2026-07-05 (no extension, petition late) or 2026-07-06. A rule must warn.

title: Bailiff's notice served inside the year: does it interrupt the limitation period

expect.why: 317 ¶1 lists what interrupts: the judicial claim, 'التنبيه' or the seizure, a claim in bankruptcy, and acts done in the proceedings. It does not say that a formal notice (إعذار) is a 'تنبيه', and the slot does not say it is a commandment to pay. If it interrupts, 319 ¶1 starts a new period of the same length when the effect ends (end of the effect not stated), so the claim is in time; if not, the last day under 312 ¶3 is 2026-03-01 and the petition is a month late (it is in time under 309 ¶1 anyway). The text does not settle this. Last day without interruption: 2026-03-01.

title: Notice by registered letter inside the year: not a judicial claim, notice or seizure

expect.why: 317 ¶1 names the judicial claim, the 'تنبيه', the seizure and acts during pleadings; a private registered letter is none of these on its words, and 318 ¶1 needs an acknowledgment by the debtor (not a slot). So interruption is unlikely, last day 2026-03-01 (312 ¶3, 314 ¶1), but wages also reach 309 ¶1 (five years) and the text does not say whether 'التنبيه' covers any notice: the text does not settle this, the rule must warn, not decide.

title: Contract made fifteen years ago less one day: the due date is not the contract date

expect.why: 308 ¶1 gives fifteen years; 315 ¶1 starts it 'من اليوم الذى يصبح فيه الدين مستحق الاداء', the day the debt falls due, not the day of the contract, and no slot holds the due date. A debt due later than the contract makes the claim in time, so a rule cannot decide from contract_date and must ask for the due date (which no slot holds). If the debt fell due on the contract date, 314 ¶1 gives last day 2026-06-15 and the petition is one day before it. lastDay left out.

title: Contract made exactly fifteen years before the petition

expect.why: Same as bc13: the starting day is the due date (315 ¶1), not the contract date, and no slot holds it. Only if the debt fell due on the contract date would the petition be on the last day (2026-06-15, 314 ¶1: first day not counted, period complete at the end of the last day). A rule must ask for the due date, not decide. lastDay left out.

title: Contract made fifteen years and one day before the petition

expect.why: As bc13: the contract date may lie before the due date (315 ¶1; also 315 ¶2: a conditional or term debt starts when the condition is met or the term ends). Only if the debt fell due at the contract date would it be one day late (last day 2026-06-15). Ask; lastDay left out. Late limitation is raised only by the debtor's plea (321 ¶1).

title: Contract made five months before the petition: in time whatever the due date

expect.why: 308 ¶1: fifteen years. A debt cannot fall due before the contract, so the starting day (315 ¶1) is on or after 2026-01-10 and the last day on or after 2041-01-10, whatever the due date. No shorter period of 309-312 is in play for a request for payment without a wage, fee or trade debt fact in the slots. lastDay left out because it depends on the due date.

title: Wage claim without the due date of the oldest wage

expect.why: The wages are asked for (requests) but wages_due_from is unknown: the starting day of the period (315 ¶1, due date; 313 ¶1 for 309: the time the creditor finishes his services) is missing. A missing fact is not a 'no'; the rule asks for wages_due_from.

title: Wage claim where the due date of the oldest wage is nearly a year back and the worker is in a notice dispute

expect.why: The starting day 2025-06-16 is not counted (314 ¶1: 'ولا يحسب اليوم الاول'); the year of 312 ¶3 is complete at the end of 2026-06-16, so on 2026-06-15 the petition is one day before the last day. A missing notice interrupts nothing and changes nothing here (317 ¶1 lists no formal notice). In time under 309 ¶1 too.
